options.label: Run the full quality gate once over the wave, then rule
options.pros: Confidence HIGH — the devils-advocate lens grounded this in a verbatim quote at plans/review/00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty.md:89 that I read and confirmed. One run answers the verify question for every plan now in review rather than for this one alone, and it produces the integrated evidence the wave's sync barrier was designed to produce but has never been observed producing — I confirmed enqueueWaveSync has no JavaScript caller anywhere in src, so that barrier has never actually run. The narrow scope is also the wave's declared division of labour rather than a private shortcut: I found the same file-scoped Step 14 in at least fourteen other plans now in review, and 00011-r2z states 'no full suite' explicitly, so rejecting this one plan for it leaves the convention untouched everywhere else.

The convention is not universal either — 00071-fg1 records a full gate pass in review — so it is a habit rather than a rule, and the contracts changed here are read by 24 test files and nine dependent plans.

The sibling 00013-r3b declares task-registry.js, task-reconcile.js AND menu-screens.js while this plan declares only the first two, so the sibling is the only plan at this gate that can make all three paths agree in one pass — and the quarantine code is marked in-comment as R3-B item 8, meaning it already belongs to that slice. Sending this plan back cannot fix the defect, because the file carrying the bypass is not in its declared list.
options.cons: It splits one hazard across two rulings, and 00013-r3b is itself sitting in review — if it crosses without the fix, nobody owns the gap and the three paths stay inconsistent with no plan left to carry it. Recording an objection against a sibling is also weaker than fixing it: that plan's reviewer has to rediscover why it matters, and this plan is meanwhile recorded done carrying a guard its own module header describes as an invariant.
options.description: I verified the bypass at src/lib/menu-screens.js:1744-1745 and its three call sites at :1838, :1880 and :2027; the quarantine filter is at src/lib/task-reconcile.js:637-649.

options.label: Make the scheduler lifecycle-aware in this plan
options.pros: One guard inside canRun and nextRunnable covers all three paths at once and cannot be bypassed by any caller that computes promote for itself, which is the property a safety invariant is supposed to have. It also puts the fix in the same commit as the defect rather than trusting a second plan and a second reviewer to carry it, and this plan does declare both scheduler files, so the change is reachable from here without widening the slice or waiting on anyone.
options.cons: It inverts the module dependency I verified: task-registry.js:773 opens the scheduler section as pure and reads only status, kind, touches and gitOp, while the orphan reason is written by task-reconcile, which calls into the scheduler at :616 and not the other way round. The scheduler's four rules and two test files are written against that narrow input contract, so this widens the rule surface at a gate to guard a path the promote projection already covers.

questions.prompt: A wave sync commits once every dependency has SETTLED, and settled includes an orphan declared dead on age alone whose own record says the agent may still be editing its files. Approve 00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty across Gate 3?

options.label: Record the precondition and leave the pure scheduler alone
options.pros: Confidence HIGH — the premortem lens grounded this in a verbatim quote at src/lib/task-registry.js:823 that I read and confirmed; the code reads exactly as claimed. Two conjuncts I verified myself make the path unopenable today: enqueueWaveSync at actions.js:1670 is the sole producer of a sync task and has no JavaScript caller anywhere in src, and Rule 2 at task-registry.js:845 refuses a sync while ANY task occupies a slot, so every other wave member must already have settled — a conjunct all three prosecution lenses omitted. Leaving the scheduler pure keeps its four rules testable in isolation rather than adding lifecycle provenance to close a path no code can currently open.
options.cons: An unreachable path is not a guarded path. The moment a wave sync is enqueued for real — and the menu instruction surface at menu.md:62 already tells the session to do it — the precondition set shrinks by one and nothing re-checks this argument then. If it ever fires the artifact is a commit of a partially-written tree, surfacing as an unexplained bad merge rather than an error. I also could not verify the defense lens's zero-occurrence task history, because .ctoc/state/tasks.json lies outside my permitted read scope and I did not open it.

options.label: Exclude age-only orphans from settling a sync barrier now
options.pros: The barrier's own premise — that the wave has settled — becomes true before a commit is taken, and it is then guarded by code rather than by the absence of an occurrence, so it stays guarded when wave syncs become routine rather than hypothetical. depsSatisfied already holds the dependency object and the orphan reason is durably recorded on result.orphanReason at task-reconcile.js:368-373, so the change is small and reachable from this plan's own declared files without waiting for a sibling.
options.cons: It puts a reconcile-authored lifecycle field into the section task-registry.js:773 declares pure, reopening both scheduler test files at the gate. A sync would then wait up to the presumed-dead bound at task-reconcile.js:414 — the kind floor times the multiplier — so the exclusion must be time-bounded or it reopens the barrier deadlock this plan was written to close.

questions.prompt: The plan states every wedge becomes a loud event, but report.unsatisfiable, report.deferred and report.stalenessOrphaned have no reader anywhere in src. Approve 00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty across Gate 3?

options.label: Ship the inbox reader with the sibling that declares the render file, and correct this plan's claim
options.pros: Confidence HIGH — the premortem lens grounded this in a verbatim quote at src/lib/menu-screens.js:243 that I read and confirmed: the dashboard renders one orphaned count and nothing else, and my own search found no reader for the three report fields outside the module that writes them. The data is already computed with its reason and dependency ids, so only a render line is missing, and 00013-r3b declares menu-screens.js while this plan does not. Correcting the claim matters on its own: a plan recorded done asserting a loud event that does not exist is the dead-producer pattern the parent vision names as a reason for this rebuild.
options.cons: It leaves the wedge unrendered for however long the sibling takes, and an unsatisfiable task is marked failed at task-reconcile.js:474 and then swept from the active view once past the retention window — so the record of a permanent dependency cycle is eventually lost, not merely quiet. Editing the plan's claim also costs a round on work that is otherwise complete, and a claim corrected downward reads worse than one that was never overstated.

options.label: Accept the reports as a computed surface a consuming slice will render
options.pros: The wedge is not invisible today: an unsatisfiable task is marked failed with its reason and dependency ids in result.summary, so it appears in the failed count and the reason is there on drill-in. Keeping the slice at two modules is also what makes its diff reviewable, and the report contract is exactly the interface a rendering slice needs — building a producer before its consumer is a normal order rather than a defect, provided the consumer actually lands.
options.cons: A permanent dependency cycle and an ordinary one-off failure render identically, so the human learns nothing about which one they are looking at, and that distinction is the entire point of the unsatisfiable detection this plan added. By CTOC's own measure — a module is done when a human can reach it — this feature is not done, and 'a consuming slice will render it' is exactly the deferral that produced the unwired machinery the vision was written to fix.

questions.prompt: The concurrent-edit guard sits in an empty catch that falls through to the unquarantined promote list and records nothing, in a file where every other failure path is loud. Approve 00003-r2a-scheduler-lifecycle-honesty across Gate 3?

options.label: Record the fault and drop the affected candidates
options.pros: Confidence HIGH — the red-team lens grounded this in a verbatim quote at src/lib/task-reconcile.js:651 that I read and confirmed; the catch body is a comment only, and the loud contrast recording report.saveFailed at :599 sits in the same function. The change keeps the render unbreakable, which is that comment's actual intent, while failing safe instead of open: a throw inside the glob overlap test currently produces exactly the concurrent edit the block exists to prevent. The project's own rules name a swallowing empty catch as a blocked pattern, and this file is one the plan declares, so it can be fixed here rather than routed to anyone.
options.cons: It needs a new report field and a fault-injection test, reopening Step 8 and both reconcile test files on a diff that four later slices have already layered onto — task-reconcile.js:302, :312, :363 and :389-410 are marked in-comment as belonging to a later slice, so an executor returning here edits around another plan's uncrossed work and the review evidence for both becomes harder to separate. The fault path may also never have fired once.

options.label: Approve with the empty catch as built
options.pros: The catch is a deliberate choice with a stated reason: the quarantine is a defensive refinement and a fault inside it must never take down the dashboard render, which is the surface the human actually depends on. Failing open restores precisely the promote behaviour that shipped before the quarantine existed, so the failure mode is a return to the prior baseline rather than a newly introduced hazard, and touchesOverlap operating over two string arrays has a narrow throw surface to begin with.
options.cons: A guard whose failure mode is silence cannot be distinguished at runtime from a guard that ran and found nothing, so nobody will ever learn that it fired. The consequence on that path is two agents editing one file, which produces no error at all — only a wrong diff — in a wave designed to run five agents concurrently.

It also asks for a wave-level run that no function schedules — the barrier is documented at actions.js:1653 and instructed at menu.md:62, but I confirmed its only producer has no JavaScript caller, so a human has to choose to run it and may simply not. If nobody does, this plan sits in review indefinitely on a condition nothing will satisfy on its own.
